title: seller-spark-notes-fallbacks-sketch
content:
Purpose: quick-reference note set for SEs/SDRs to run 30s/90s/3-min pitches and handle runtime fallback objections during pilots. Not polished — living doc for rapid rehearsal and pocket reference.

High-level thesis (one line): show value fast, then neutralize operational risk fears with simple fallback stories and measurable thresholds.

Top-line hooks (30s / 90s / 3-min)
- 30s: "Redwood makes inference predictable — same API across hosted, reserved, and private so you can ship features now and scale later without rework." (Follow-up: ask "what's top metric you need to protect?")
- 90s: Bulletize outcomes: latency SLOs (regional hosted < 120ms median), reserved capacity for predictable throughput (committed GPUs + burst), private for compliance — highlight cost control levers (batching, cache, quantization). End with one ask: "Can I map one customer workflow to these three levers in 15 minutes?"
- 3-min: Quick architecture sketch:
  * Frontend -> Redwood API (routing policy: latency pref -> hosted; cost pref -> dedicated)
  * Runtime: KV prefix cache + continuous batching -> token cost down 25–45% on typical chat workloads
  * Fallback flows: model variant (quantized lower-cost), region fallback, and queued-burst on reserved pool
  Close: propose a 2-week pilot focused on one high-value endpoint.

Rapid fallback scripts (seller language)
- Objection: "What if latency spikes under load?"
  - Reply: "We measure at token-level and have an automatic fallback path — if latency exceeds your SLA threshold the router fails over to a cheaper but compatible model or alternate region, and we continue serving while ops triages. In pilot we simulate/validate the canary for you."
- Objection: "We're worried about cost blowouts."
  - Reply: "We start with a reserved cap + adaptive batching and exact token analytics for the pilot; you get per-route burn rates and an on-call alert for anomaly spend. We can enforce hard caps for the first 30 days."
- Objection: "We need data residency."
  - Reply: "We offer a private deployment option with a customer-controlled VPC and optional on-prem package — pilot scope can be limited to specific regions or dedicated nodes."

Seller triage checklist for pilot kickoff (10 items)
1) Define 1 primary API route to pilot (single endpoint).
2) SLA target (p50/p95 latency), desired throughput (rps), and cost per 1k tokens target.
3) Model spec: family, max sequence length, expected prompt/response token mix.
4) Data residency/compliance flags.
5) Security: KMS/HSM required? audit logs?
6) Canary policy: fallback model variant and region order.
7) Monitoring: which logs/metrics customer wants in Console retention window.
8) Escalation path: who on SE/SRE will be on-call for pilot day 0–7.
9) Success criteria: latency, error rate < X, cost within Y% of estimate.
10) Optional: run a 1-hour synthetic load test to baseline.

Quick technical fallback matrix (words only)
- Condition: Cluster saturation / queued requests increasing -> Action: Route to reserved pool or quantized variant; enable strict batching thresholds; queue excess requests with retry policy.
- Condition: Model quality regression on canary -> Action: Roll back to previous model version, mark flagged prompt set, run lightweight A/B on withheld prompt test set.
- Condition: Region outage -> Action: Automatic routing to next region (same model family) with client-side timeouts adjusted; notify customer via integration.

Pilot-run playbook (week-by-week)
- Week 0: Align scope, configure API route, baseline synthetic test.
- Week 1: Live pilot with low traffic + observability enabled; run golden prompt set every 6 hours.
- Week 2: Scale traffic stepwise to target throughput; validate cost and failover behavior; handoff ops runbook.
- Post-pilot: deliver short exec summary with measured token cost, latency SLO attainment, and a recommended next-step (Dedicated/Private).

Pocket-level metrics to call out in conversation
- Median token latency (ms), p95 latency (ms), tokens per request, cost per 1k tokens, queue length, model version drift score (if available).

Sample email follow-up after demo
Subject: Quick summary + 1-step next: pilot scope
Body: "Great to chat today — here are the 3 things we promised: 1) baseline synthetic with your prompt set, 2) a 2-week pilot on hosted with a canary fallback plan, 3) a post-pilot economic brief. Next step: can we lock the primary endpoint and SLA target?"

Open items / TODOs (internal)
- Add concrete numbers for median/p95 from our hosted catalog for the most common model families. (Action: Marcus)
- Create a short script for ops to run the synthetic golden prompt every 4 hours during pilot. (Action: Evan)
- Validate legal checklist items for private deployment pilots in EMEA. (Action: Rina)

Risks and mitigation notes (talking points)
- Risk: Pilot shows quality drift between hosted and quantized variants -> Mitigate by running prompt-specific evaluation and thresholding quantization recommendations; offer human-in-loop fallbacks for first 48 hours.
- Risk: Unexpected spend spike -> Mitigate by enforcing committed reserved capacity or admin hard caps and real-time spend alerts.

One-pager summary (to paste into Slack)
"Seller Spark: kickoff pilots that prove latency & cost predictability. Show 30s/90s hooks, align one endpoint+SLA, enable automatic routing + fallback policy, run week-by-week pilot, deliver token-level economics and ops handoff."

Notes to self: keep this under 1 page for field use. When polishing, add a tiny visual for routing policy and an ordered script for canary rollback steps.

Version history: rough notes — iter 0 created 2024-11-15, iter 1 internal edits 2024-12-10, iter 2 added triage checklist 2025-01-08, iter 3 content hygiene 2025-01-18 (current).
